title: How The World Learned To Love Fast Food

blanks.sentence: Major fast food brands are described as _____.
The episode focuses on the _____ of fast food.
Many founders did not have a _____.
Fast food made business _____ easier for ordinary people.
A can-do attitude includes confidence and _____.
The American dream links success to _____ and determination.
Today, two McDonald’s restaurants far apart can serve exactly the _____.
The financial crash helped cause McDonald’s final _____ in Iceland.

multipleChoice.question: What historical development is the programme mainly discussing?
options: How fast food spread globally from mid-century America
Why British people stopped eating fast food
How home cooking replaced restaurant chains
Why all fast food brands began in Iceland

multipleChoice.question: Which foods are given as examples of cheap and easy American fast food?
options: Pizza, pasta and salads
Soup, rice and vegetables
Fish, chips and tea
Hamburgers, French fries and milkshakes

multipleChoice.question: What does Adam Chandler suggest about early fast-food founders?
options: They usually came from wealthy academic families
They could succeed without traditional educational advantages
They mainly worked outside the United States
They avoided joining established systems

multipleChoice.question: Why is the phrase “at the heart of the story” explained?
options: To introduce a medical problem caused by fast food
To show that fast food was unpopular after the war
To identify the key idea behind fast food’s rise
To argue that the story is mainly about recipes

multipleChoice.question: What does a can-do attitude involve?
options: Confidence and determination to solve problems
Refusing to follow any system
Waiting for others to provide money
Avoiding new challenges

multipleChoice.question: Why did fast food brands connect with the American dream?
options: They made success depend on family background
They promised success without effort
They were limited to one social class
They suggested ordinary people could succeed through work

multipleChoice.question: What does the example of two McDonald’s on opposite sides of the planet show?
options: Menus change completely in each country
The brand offers a highly standardised product
Fast food is no longer available in America
Customers must travel far to eat the meal

multipleChoice.question: How did Iceland differ from places where McDonald’s was easily accepted?
options: It had no local food traditions
It welcomed every foreign chain warmly
It gave McDonald’s a cold reception
It banned all burger restaurants immediately

multipleChoice.question: Why is the shalpuborgari mentioned?
options: To show Iceland already had its own version of a burger
To prove Iceland copied McDonald’s exactly
To explain why burgers were unknown in Iceland
To describe McDonald’s most popular product

multipleChoice.question: What does McDonald’s experience in Iceland imply?
options: Global brands always succeed everywhere
Financial crises help fast food chains expand
Local food culture has no effect on foreign chains
Local habits and economic shocks can limit global brands
